approach: xtask `ci` decides reuse in Rust: fingerprint HEAD with athena-git's existing `attrs::fingerprint` (the gate's own function), reuse only a well-formed marker naming that exact fingerprint, otherwise run fmt/clippy/test and write the marker only after all pass. ci.yml keeps one always-running job 'fmt, clippy, tests' (never skipped, no ruleset change). On push runs it restores/saves the marker with actions/cache keyed only `ci-pass-<fingerprint>` (saved only after a full pass on a miss). A pull_request run cannot read the branch-scoped entry, so for same-repo athena/* heads it asks GitHub for CI's own push-run result for the identical sha (job 'fmt, clippy, tests', event push, conclusion success). Only an exact success writes the marker; failure, skipped, missing, timeout or API error write nothing, so the full checks run. gh.rs gains a best-effort `push_candidate_early` through the `Remote` seam at verification start, and a lease-guarded `Remote::replace` that publish uses only for the job's own branch when the remote head equals the early candidate.

decisions.choice: Reuse decision lives in xtask Rust (pure decide(fingerprint, marker_text), marker_text, read_marker with any io/utf8 error -> none); ci.yml only restores/saves/creates the marker file.
decisions.reason: Trust rules become testable with cargo test -p xtask; missing, failed, malformed or unreadable marker means full checks.

rejected.option: Job-level skip on a cache hit
rejected.why: A skipped required job reports success without proof.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 6: do NOT skip the pull_request job. It always runs under the required name. For same-repo athena/* heads a step looks up the push run of the same sha via the GitHub API and writes the marker only on a conclusion of success for the job 'fmt, clippy, tests'; anything else leaves no marker and the full checks run. Other PRs (human, fork) run the full job as before.
decisions.reason: The pull_request run reads refs/pull/N/merge and base-branch caches, never the head branch, and the PR does not exist at early-push time, so it can never hit the branch cache. The push run on the same sha can (same branch scope). Using CI's own push-run result on the identical sha lets the required check be a real run that passes only on proof, so the ruleset is never satisfied by a skip. Failed push run, missing run or timeout yields the full build.

rejected.option: Job-level skip of the pull_request run for athena/* (previous plan)
rejected.why: A skipped job counts as success for the ruleset and weakens the required check (finding 6).

rejected.option: Push run also saves under a key the pull_request run can read
rejected.why: That would be the base branch or merge-ref scope; writing main's shared caches from branches is out of scope.

rejected.option: Open the PR at verification start and save on pull_request runs
rejected.why: Needs a Host change and PR opening before verification passes; much larger.
A new required name would change the ruleset; out of scope.

decisions.choice: Fingerprint rules commit: use HEAD for both treeish and rules commit, as the plan before, but justified and tested: athena-gate (invariant.rs) judges a commit with the rules of its first parent, which differ from HEAD's only when the commit itself edits the rules; CI uses HEAD's own rules, which is stricter-or-equal for reuse because a rules edit changes the tree. Add an xtask test where a commit changes the rules file (athena-exclude/owner attribute) and the fingerprint changes so the result is not reused.
decisions.reason: CI has no base commit; the fingerprint definition itself is unchanged (attrs::fingerprint reused, not reimplemented). Any fingerprint error means a full run.

rejected.option: Use the first parent as rules commit
rejected.why: The cache is written by one commit and read by a different one (candidate vs landing), so the parent differs and keys would not match.
Duplicates classification rules; hashFiles over-includes records/.

decisions.choice: Cache key exactly ci-pass-<fingerprint>, no restore-keys; marker content 'athena-ci-pass v1 <fingerprint>'; save only on push events, only after xtask ci succeeds, only on a restore miss. Existing toolchain/registry/target saves stay default-branch only; no step reads records/. Trust model stated in a comment.
decisions.reason: Exact key plus a self-naming marker refuses a wrong restore; failures never save; main's shared caches untouched by branches.

rejected.why: Merge-ref scope is unreadable by the push run.

rejected.option: Trust an Athena record or check result

decisions.choice: push_candidate_early(remote, ancestry, job, candidate) -> EarlyPush guarded by check_push on work_branch(job); any refusal or error becomes a returned warning. Called from run.rs at verification start (before the verifier snapshot) when origin exists.
decisions.reason: Overlaps the push run with verification; verification never depends on it (criterion 4).

rejected.option: Push at the start of land --pr
rejected.why: Verification has finished; saves no time.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 8: add Remote::replace(branch, commit, expected) (force-with-lease pinned to expected). A new check_replace accepts only work_branch(job) and refuses every other branch (main, other jobs' branches). publish calls replace only when remote_head == early_candidate is checked explicitly first; otherwise the normal check_push path refuses non-descendants. Tests: replace refuses a non-job branch; refuses on a lease mismatch (FakeRemote head != expected); a human-fix head is never overwritten; the matching early candidate is replaced.
decisions.reason: Landing builds its own commit that does not descend from the candidate, so a plain push would be refused. The branch restriction, explicit equality and lease narrow the widened posture to one case.

rejected.option: Make landing build on the candidate
rejected.why: Changes land.rs history rules; much larger.
Cache scope must be the landing branch.

decisions.choice: Files outside the five listed (findings 1-5, 9): keep, each diff minimal. xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock only add the athena-git dependency so xtask reuses attrs::fingerprint instead of duplicating it; run.rs is the only place verification start exists; test_support.rs and external_calls.rs only get the new LandPr field and the new Remote method so the workspace compiles.
decisions.reason: Reuse and criterion 4 cannot be met inside the five files alone; the user's reading says to reuse existing fingerprint code and push at verification start.

rejected.option: Put the verification-start call inside gh.rs only
rejected.why: gh.rs does not own verification start; nothing would call it.

decisions.choice: Do not change the ruleset, job name, fingerprint definition or main's cache writing.

steps: Add athena-git to xtask/Cargo.toml; in xtask/src/main.rs add governed_fingerprint (attrs::fingerprint of HEAD with HEAD rules), marker_text, read_marker, decide, decide_push_run, and a ci-fingerprint subcommand.

Write xtask tests: scratch-repo records/owner/governed/rules-change cases, marker failure cases, push-run conclusion cases, failing runner writes no marker, and the ci.yml shape test.

Edit the first job of ci.yml: fingerprint step, marker restore, same-repo athena/* pull_request lookup of the push run (writes marker only on success), xtask ci with the marker path, push-only save on miss after the run, trust comment; no job-level skip; leave other jobs and existing saves untouched.

In gh.rs add Remote::replace (GitRemote uses push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<expected>), check_replace (job branch only), push_candidate_early, LandPr.early_candidate, and the publish branch requiring remote_head == early_candidate then check_replace; update FakeRemote, NoRemote, test_support; write the gh.rs tests.

risks.risk: Landing push refused after the early push because the landing commit does not descend from the candidate.
risks.mitigation: Lease-guarded replace limited to work_branch(job), used only when remote head equals the early candidate; tests show other heads, other branches and lease mismatches are refused.

risks.risk: Stale or poisoned cache entry or a mistaken push-run lookup makes CI pass without checks.
risks.mitigation: Exact key, no restore-keys, self-naming marker, strict parse, save only after a full pass; lookup accepts only conclusion success for the same sha, event push, this repo; all tested.

risks.risk: pull_request run waits on a push run that never starts or is slow, adding time.
risks.mitigation: Bounded poll, then full checks; never a pass without success proof.

risks.risk: Early push triggers CI on a candidate that later fails verification.
risks.mitigation: Only the job's own athena/<job> branch; failure is a warning; cost bounded to one run.

risks.risk: Adding athena-git to xtask breaks --locked or setup.
risks.mitigation: Refresh Cargo.lock once, confirm only xtask's dependency entry changed, run the three checks.

risks.risk: Fingerprint fails in CI (shallow or detached checkout).
risks.mitigation: Checkout uses fetch-depth 0; any fingerprint error falls to the full run.

demonstrations.method: xtask unit tests build scratch git repos (athena-git test style) with records/ and an owner path marked athena-exclude. Store the marker for HEAD's fingerprint; commit a records/-and-owner-only change: fingerprint equal and decide returns Reuse. Commit a governed source change: fingerprint differs and decide returns RunFull. A commit editing the rules file also changes the fingerprint.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the fingerprint did not ignore records/owner paths the records-only case would differ; if reuse ignored the fingerprint the governed case would return Reuse.

demonstrations.method: decide is called with no marker, empty, 'fail' marker, malformed, truncated, a marker naming another fingerprint, and a directory at the marker path read through the real read_marker; run_ci with a failing runner writes no marker and returns an error; a pure decide_push_run(conclusion) helper maps only exact 'success' to a marker and failure/skipped/cancelled/none/garbage to none.
demonstrations.observes: Every bad case yields RunFull / no marker; a failing run leaves no marker; only the exact well-formed marker yields Reuse.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a missing/failed/malformed marker or a skipped/failed push run counted as pass, the assertion would see Reuse and fail.

demonstrations.method: A workflow-shape test reads .github/workflows/ci.yml and asserts: job name 'fmt, clippy, tests'; the job has no `if` that skips the pull_request event; the marker key is 'ci-pass-' plus the fingerprint step output with no restore-keys; the save step requires push and a miss and comes after the xtask ci step; the push-run lookup step writes the marker only on conclusion success and only for same-repo athena/* heads; no step mentions records/; a trust-model comment exists; the existing shared-cache saves keep their default-branch-only condition. Reviewer also reads the ci.yml diff.
demonstrations.observes: The shape test passes on the edited ci.yml.
demonstrations.fails_without: Adding restore-keys, a job-level skip, saving on pull_request, or loosening the shared saves fails an assertion.

demonstrations.method: gh.rs tests with an extended FakeRemote (replace, optional push error) and fake Host: (a) push_candidate_early pushes exactly (work_branch(job), candidate) once; (b) a push error or refused branch returns a warning, not an error; (c) publish replaces only when the remote head equals the early candidate, and replace refuses other branches and lease mismatches, a human-fix head is not overwritten and landing is refused; (d) land_pr after the early push still calls wait_for_checks, host.checks gets the landing commit, and merge is not requested while checks are pending.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the early push the push list is empty; if failures propagated the failure test sees Err; without the guarded replace landing over the candidate is refused; if checks were polled on the candidate the head assertion fails.

open_questions: Files outside the five listed (xtask/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, run.rs, test_support.rs, external_calls.rs) are needed; confirm acceptable.

Does the existing ci.yml grant a token able to read workflow runs? The lookup step needs actions: read on this job only; if the workflow-level permissions are narrower the producer adds that one scope. If the lookup cannot work, the pull_request run simply runs the full checks (safe, but no speedup).

How long should the lookup wait for the push run? Plan: poll up to about 10 minutes for the same sha, then fall through to the full checks; the value is a producer choice, to be noted in decisions.md.
The brief says 'Host seam'; Host/PrHost have no push, so the plan uses the Remote trait.
ci-routing section 4.1 was not read; the cache-scope reasoning relies on the brief and GitHub's documented scope rules.

Whether a push-event job and a pull_request job of the same name on one sha both count toward the ruleset was not settled from the repo; both must pass, so safety does not depend on it, and the After measurement will show the speedup.
